overview: Linkage keeps genes together during inheritance; crossing over is the process that can break that linkage.
genZNote: Linkage: genes carpooling together. Crossing over: someone swaps seats mid-ride.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: The tendency of genes located close together on the same chromosome to be inherited together.
aspects.valueB: The exchange of genetic material between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes during meiosis I.

aspects.label: Effect on Recombination
aspects.valueA: Reduces the frequency of new gene combinations (recombinant offspring).
aspects.valueB: Increases genetic variation by creating new allele combinations.

aspects.label: Distance Dependence
aspects.valueA: Stronger linkage when genes are physically closer together on a chromosome.
aspects.valueB: Crossover frequency increases with distance between genes — the basis of genetic mapping.

aspects.label: When It Occurs
aspects.valueA: A description of inheritance pattern, not a specific event.
aspects.valueB: Occurs specifically during prophase I (pachytene stage) of meiosis.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Crossover frequency between two genes is used to calculate map distance in genetic linkage maps.
overlay.memoryTrick: Linkage keeps genes stuck together; crossing over is what un-sticks them.
overlay.commonMisconception: Complete linkage (no crossing over at all) is rare — most linked genes still show some recombination.
